AERB Radiation Safety — The India-Specific RT Gate

Industrial radiography in India requires AERB licensing under the Atomic Energy Act + AERB Safety Code AERB/SC/IR-1 — Radiation Safety Officer (RSO) per ISTR-1 + Radiographer per ISTR-2 + Radiographer's Assistant per ISTR-3. Foreign certifications do not substitute. Atlantis Hyderabad bundles AERB RSO + ISTR prep alongside ASNT/ISO 9712 RT — critical for inspectors mobilising to Reliance Jamnagar, IOCL Paradip, NTPC Vindhyachal, ONGC offshore, HAL Bengaluru.

What drives NDT training demand in Hyderabad

Hyderabad has become India's aerospace manufacturing city: Tata's aerostructure joint ventures build fuselage and wing assemblies for global OEMs, Safran and GE run engine-component plants, and defence programmes cluster around the DRDO missile complex — all of it under aerospace NDT rules — alongside pharma equipment fabrication and the NTPC power belt to the north. Every one of those assets is examined on intervals set by code, and the examinations must be performed by certified personnel — which is what creates continuous local demand for qualified technicians, and continuous pressure on employers to develop them.

Which methods to train first in this market

Training investment should follow the local work. In Hyderabad that means eddy current above all, PT on components, and UT for composites — under NAS 410 / EN 4179 rules; in the fabrication sector, VT to CWI-style acceptance first, then UT and RT for coded work; and where power work features, UT including phased array on rotors and headers, MT during outages, and eddy current on condenser tubing. A candidate who certifies against what local employers actually examine is employable months sooner than one who spreads across every method thinly.

Which certification scheme employers here expect

Aerospace work runs under NAS 410 / EN 4179 personnel requirements with OEM (Nadcap-audited) special-process approval — a different regime from industrial NDT entirely; industrial plant follows IBR for boilers and ISNT (NCB) or ASNT certification in contracts.

For a candidate this decides the route before any course is booked: train toward the scheme your target employers name in their contracts. Where both employer-based (SNT-TC-1A) and central (ISO 9712 / PCN) certification circulate, the central certificate travels with you between employers — worth weighing against the faster employer-based route. How ASNT certification works · ISO 9712 vs SNT-TC-1A.

Levels, honestly explained

Level I performs calibrations and examinations under supervision — the entry point, usually reached in one method first. Level II sets up, interprets against the code and signs the report; it is the level contracts in Hyderabad actually specify. Level III writes and approves procedures and qualifies the Level I/IIs — the level a growing inspection function eventually needs to own or engage. Progression is training hours plus documented experience hours, so anyone already working under supervision moves faster than a cold start.
